new_findings_today.title: /api/chat returns HTTP 500 for every valid question — the AI chat feature is completely down, on both the simple (Haiku) and complex (Sonnet) routing paths
new_findings_today.detail: 5 diagnostic probes today, all with real, well-formed questions, all failed identically with {"error":"Something went wrong"} at HTTP 500: 'Best time to visit Leh?' (x3, ~2.7-3.3s), 'What is the weather like in Goa in December?' (~2.8s), 'hello' (~2.2s), and one complex question ('Compare Manali vs Shimla for a family trip, pros and cons', ~7.0s — this one routes to the isComplexQuestion=true / model='claude-sonnet-4-6' branch instead of the simple/Haiku branch). This is DISTINCT from DEEP-Phase7-A1, which covers malformed/oversized-input handling and is still correctly closed (malformed->400, empty->400, wrong_shape->400, oversized->413) — the input-validation guards work fine; the failure is in the successful-request path that used to return a real answer. Investigated and ruled out: (1) hybrid_search and match_documents Postgres RPC functions both exist with signatures matching what the route code calls (query_text/query_embedding/match_count/keyword_weight/semantic_weight) — not a missing-function issue; (2) no commit to apps/web since 07-20 (or to package.json/package-lock.json anywhere in the repo since before 07-13) touches api/chat/route.ts, its imports, or the @anthropic-ai/sdk (^0.88.0) / openai (^6.34.0) versions — ruled out as a code or dependency regression from this week's deploys; (3) chat_logs shows real users successfully using chat as recently as 2026-07-22 15:26:55-15:31:51 UTC (4 real conversational turns, all answered) and 'Best time to visit Leh?' specifically succeeding on both 07-13 and 07-20's own QA probes — so the break happened sometime in the 07-22 15:31 UTC to now window, with no code change in that window that explains it. One code smell worth a direct check even though it doesn't fully explain today's reproduction: apps/web/src/app/api/chat/route.ts line 388 hardcodes model='claude-sonnet-4-6' for complex questions, a string that does not match current Anthropic model-naming (current lineup: claude-opus-5/claude-sonnet-5/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001/claude-fable-5) and may be a retired or invalid model ID — but the simple/Haiku path uses model='claude-haiku-4-5-20251001' (a currently-valid ID) and fails identically, so a bad model string on the complex path cannot be the sole cause; the complex path's longer failure latency (~7.0s vs ~2.2-3.5s for simple) is consistent with it failing differently/later, which would fit two separate problems (an invalid model on the complex path, plus something else — most plausibly an API key/auth/quota issue — breaking the simple path too), but this QA harness has no visibility into the actual thrown error or Anthropic-side response to confirm which.
new_findings_today.evidence: 5x curl -X POST https://www.nakshiq.com/api/chat, all returning {"error":"Something went wrong"} status=500. Timings: 3.35s, 2.78s, 2.72s ('Best time to visit Leh?' x3 across two batches), 2.24s ('hello'), 6.96s ('Compare Manali vs Shimla...'). DEEP-Phase7-A1 malformed-input probes all correctly 400/413 in the same session. pg_proc check: hybrid_search(query_text text, query_embedding vector, match_count integer, keyword_weight double precision, semantic_weight double precision) and match_documents(query_embedding vector, match_count integer, filter_type text) both present. chat_logs SELECT ... ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 8 shows last successful answer 2026-07-22T15:31:51.16Z; 0 chat_logs rows from today (consistent with 0/5 successes). git log --since 2026-07-20 -- apps/web/ = 7 commits (b32e3a160, 2976b6d8b, 03d1fe440, 0f76b526c, dc540e771, ad59b0904, 68fa0e37a), none touching api/chat/route.ts or its dependencies; git log since 07-13 on package.json/package-lock.json anywhere in repo = 0 commits.
new_findings_today.recommendation: Check Vercel's function runtime logs for /api/chat directly — this QA harness can only see the generic 500 response body (the route's catch-all swallows the real error into console.error('Chat error:', err), which isn't visible from outside), so the actual thrown error/status is the fastest path to root cause. In parallel, directly verify ANTHROPIC_API_KEY validity/quota/rate-limit status on the Anthropic console, and separately reconsider the hardcoded model='claude-sonnet-4-6' string on line 388 of apps/web/src/app/api/chat/route.ts regardless of today's specific root cause — it does not match current model-naming and is worth updating to a current model ID (e.g. claude-sonnet-5) on its own merits. This is the AI product's flagship differentiating feature and it is fully non-functional for every visitor right now.

new_findings_today.title: Site-wide elevated TTFB today (all 10/10 sampled destinations, most core routes) — confirmed as cold ISR/CDN cache from 2 deploys landing 9-17 minutes before this run started, not a regression
new_findings_today.detail: Unlike prior runs where only 1-2 long-tail destinations showed cold-start TTFB, today ALL 10 sampled destinations were elevated (2210-4726ms, vs the usual 600-1000ms range) and most Section-I core routes were also elevated (798-2031ms vs 07-20's 68-763ms). This tracks with the deploy timeline: the 03d1fe440 and 2976b6d8b commits deployed at approximately 01:51 and 01:59 UTC, and this QA run started probing at 02:08:46 UTC — only 9-17 minutes later, likely before the CDN/ISR cache had been repopulated by real traffic. Re-requesting 3 of the slowest destination pages (courtallam, harihareshwar, theur) and 3 of the slowest core routes (/en/festivals, /en/treks, /hi/explore) all returned x-vercel-cache: HIT at 123-235ms on the second hit, confirming this is the documented 'every prod deploy resets the ISR cache' behavior (explicitly called out in commit ad59b0904's message) operating at a wider scale than usual simply because today's deploy was unusually close in time to this QA run, not because more of the catalogue has become slow to serve.

new_findings_today.recommendation: No action needed. If a future run shows this same site-wide pattern WITHOUT a same-day deploy to explain it, that would be worth investigating as an actual regression.
